topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's scope, recaps histological practicals, and outlines the learning objectives on oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and genetic instability.

topics.label: Tumor Virology and the Cellular Origins of Oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: They trace the historical discovery of tumor viruses and how studying their transforming mechanisms revealed that oncogenes originate from captured and mutated normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: It details the laboratory assays and cell culture methods used to evaluate whether specific genes or mutations can drive cellular transformation and tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Classification of Cancer Mutations and Cell Cycle Control
topics.groupedBecause: They define oncogenic versus tumor-suppressive mutations and explain how these alterations disrupt cell cycle checkpoints and gene function through mechanisms like dominant-negative effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Cellular Effects of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: The Multistep Model of Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the Vogelstein model illustrating how the stepwise accumulation and timing of mutations in oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes drive cancer progression from normal tissue to malignancy.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss how inheriting germline mutations accelerates tumorigenesis across specific familial syndromes and how secondary mutations can drive ongoing tumor evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session by referencing the learning outcomes, suggesting supplementary reading, and previewing the next lecture.
